To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EGFR mutations can occur in multiple lung tumors from the same patient and that k-ras mutation and chromosomal aberration analysis can help in defining their relationship.

(1) in one of our patients, a deletion of exon 19 in EGFR was present at all tumor sites, and a similar pattern of copy number aberrations was observed, suggesting that they shared the same clonal origins; and (2) in the other two cases we identified different k-ras genotypic and copy number aberration patterns, suggesting different underlying tumorigenic pathways.
the molecular analysis of multiple lung lesions in patients with multiple lung tumors can be useful in defining the relationship between these tumors.

the molecular characterization of multiple neoplastic lesions of the lung in order to better understand their relationship.
the molecular characterization of lung cancer in the context of multiple neoplastic lesions in the lung.

a single patient may have multiple tumors with different genotypes and/or different pathways of tumorigenicity, and therefore, the treatment strategy should be tailored to each individual tumor.
in one of our patients the different lung lesions were clonally related and that the other two patients presented with multiple tumors that were genetically heterogeneous.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in one case, the tumors were clonally related and in the other two cases the tumors were not clonally related.

the presence of a common EGFR mutation in all tumor sites suggests that these tumors share a common origin, whereas the presence of a k-ras mutation in only one tumor site and a distinct pattern of chromosomal alterations in the other tumor sites indicates a different origin of these lesions.

the presence of a similar pattern of EGFR mutations and chromosomal copy number alterations suggests that the different tumors are of the same clonal nature, whereas the presence of distinct k-ras mutations and chromosomal aberration pattern suggests a different clonal origin for the different tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic heterogeneity observed in patients with multiple neoplastic lung lesions should be taken into account when planning the treatment strategy.
